technical_and_design_decisions: Reuse the existing DeploymentService interface to add domain lifecycle operations (deploy/undeploy/redeploy) and overload deploy(Application) with a properties map parameter to keep API backward compatible.

Model a 'Domain' as a first-class deployable artifact that owns a set of deployed Applications, stored in a shared in-memory/cluster-aware repository so redeploy can diff and update child apps atomically.

Author AMQP transport as an XSD-defined module (camel/amqp-style) that generates namespace-aware Spring beans, so U4/U6 are satisfied by a single schema artifact and IDE tooling (xmlbeans) gets autocompletion for free.
Provide the project skeleton as a Maven Archetype (mvn-archetype) with placeholder flows, connectors, and a shared configuration block referencing the AMQP namespace defined in U6.

Implement U7 as a service-activator/bridge that continuously polls the broker queue and dispatches MuleEvents to inbound flows, and U8 as a requestor/MessageReceiver that consumes a single message on demand within a flow.
Use a common AMQP connector configuration bean (id, host, port, credentials, virtualHost) declared once at the top-level config and referenced via the new namespace from U6 to avoid duplication.
Persist domain metadata and per-app override property maps in the existing Mule deployment registry; use Mule's standard object store so it works in HA/clustered deployments.
assumptions: The work is implemented by a single experienced Mule/Java developer (assumed 6-8 hours of effective coding per workday).
Mule core 3.x DeploymentService already exists; this increment extends it rather than rebuilding it from scratch.
A broker abstraction (e.g., RabbitMQ via amqp-client) is already available or included as a transitive test dependency; no broker protocol implementation is required.
The XSD is consumed via Spring/xmlbeans which is the standard Mule module packaging mechanism; no custom IDE plugin is built, only schemas that the IDE auto-discovers.
Unit and integration tests run against a local/in-memory broker; no full multi-node cluster test harness is built.

U3 (specs review) is interpreted as producing/updating the public-facing specification documents (e.g., Markdown/Confluence + a simple review feedback template) rather than building a commenting web app.
All times are pure development effort; meetings, code reviews, and waiting time are excluded from the reported hours.

activities.activity_description: Extend DeploymentService with deployDomain, undeployDomain and redeployDomain operations. Add a DomainRepository that tracks domain -> applications mapping, cascading undeploy and atomic redeploy (stop apps, swap artifacts, restart apps). Add corresponding MBean/JMX management hooks and unit tests.

Overload DeploymentService.deploy with a deployment-override-properties parameter (Map<String,String>) and thread it through to the application's property-placeholder configuration so values supplied at deploy time win over packaged values. Add unit and integration tests covering precedence and missing-key fallback.

Produce/refresh the markdown spec documents for the AMQP transport, the base skeleton and the domain deployment feature, publish them under docs/, and add a short CONTRIBUTING-style feedback template (e.g., GitHub issues or a markdown form) so community members can review and comment.

Design and author the amqp.xsd schema covering connector, endpoint, and message-receiver element types with attribute groups, default values and documentation annotations. Wire the schema into the module so IDEs (IntelliJ, Eclipse) pick it up via META-INF/spring.schemas and offer autocompletion and validation.

Create a Maven archetype project (mule-project-skeleton) containing agreed placeholder structure: src/main/app, src/main/resources/config, transactional template, sample flow with AMQP endpoint placeholders, a parent POM that pulls in the AMQP module and a hello-world test flow. Validate by generating a project from the archetype and running it.

Refactor AMQP transport registration to expose a single top-level namespace and a reusable <amqp:connector> definition pattern. Update existing samples/tests to demonstrate declaring the connector once and referencing it from many flows. Ensure the XSD from A4 supports the global/bean reuse pattern.

Implement an inbound message receiver that registers a consumer on the configured queue, creates a MuleEvent per message and dispatches it into the configured flow. Handle acknowledgements, redelivery, error routing, and connection recovery. Add unit tests with a stubbed channel and integration tests against a test broker.

Implement an outbound message processor / <amqp:consume> component usable inside a flow that fetches a single message (with optional timeout) and returns it as a MuleMessage payload. Add unit and integration tests covering empty-queue, timeout and payload transformation cases.

Wire all features together in a sample domain that deploys an app using the skeleton, the central AMQP config, both continuous and instant consumers, and property overrides. Add a CI job (Maven) running unit and integration tests on every push.

Write usage docs: how to deploy/undeploy/redeploy a domain, how to override properties, AMQP namespace reference (auto-generated from XSD), continuous vs instant consumer cookbook, and a getting-started for the archetype.
